Overview

One task, seen from the head and both hands

RoboPose is an iPhone app for collecting task demonstrations for robot learning. Three devices, mounted on the head, left hand and right hand, record video, depth, and device position and orientation. The recordings are aligned in time so the scene and movements can be used together for training and evaluation.

The app handles device connections, readiness checks, scheduled recording and file export. The exported files are processed with the existing HoMMI framework to produce a single demonstration dataset.

Device setup

iPhones on the head and both hands

The Head iPhone is mounted on a cap, while the Left and Right iPhones sit in gripper holders. The ultrawide cameras capture ArUco tags on the gripper fingers. These tags are used during processing to calculate how far the gripper is open.

The Head iPhone acts as the recording controller (Master), and the two hand-mounted iPhones join as recording devices (Slaves). The Master creates a session for each recording and schedules its start and stop times. The Slaves join that session and save their own video and sensor data. Recordings include standard and ultrawide video, depth, ARKit poses and diagnostic logs.

Synchronization

Clock alignment, shared space and scheduled recording

The devices estimate the differences between their clocks and exchange ARKit collaboration data. Recording starts and stops at scheduled times. After recording, the files are aligned over their shared time interval.

Clock offsets and implementation details

Estimating the offset
t₀: ping sent · t₁: received by peer · t₂: pong sent · t₃: received locallyoffset = ((t₁ − t₀) + (t₂ − t₃)) / 2RTT = max(0, (t₃ − t₀) − (t₂ − t₁))
Converting scheduled times
Local scheduled time = received Master time − offsetSubtract the offset to account for how far the peer’s clock is ahead of the local clock.
Exporting files
If an offset to the connected Master is available, it is applied to the Slave’s video, depth and pose timestamps. Otherwise, the recorded timestamps are left unchanged.
Shared-space status
The World indicator updates based on whether ARKit collaboration data has been received. The Master coordinates recording; it does not define the spatial origin.

June 9, 2026 · App screens

From calibration to export

Record the gripper calibration first, then choose the calibration to use for the task demonstration. Connect the three devices, check that they are ready, and start recording.

01

Choose roles and recording type

Assign Master or Slave roles and Head, Left or Right mounting positions. After calibration, switch to Demonstration and select the saved calibration run.

The session name links the three devices’ files to the same recording.

02

Check connections and sensors

One screen shows how many devices have joined and how many video and pose records have been captured. Tracking, Sync and World badges show each device’s tracking, clock synchronization and shared-space status.

03

Schedule and record

The Master schedules the start and stop times, while each device records locally. Sensor counters and connection status remain visible on screen.

Capture Timeline logs the first video frame, depth frame and pose, along with connection changes, to help locate problems during recording.

04

Export completed recordings

Select a recording marked Ready, then choose Export Selected. The app bundles video, depth, poses and metadata. Use the iOS share sheet to send the files with AirDrop or save them to Files.

June 9, 2026 · Calibration and processing

Link a gripper calibration to the demonstration

Calibration recordings use ultrawide video with the gripper tags in view. Each demonstration file includes the name of its calibration recording, allowing calibration and demonstration files to be processed together even when their session names differ.

ArUco tag detection in the calibration video
GripperTag IDsFrames with both tags detected
Left6 / 757 / 141
Right0 / 170 / 132

The Head calibration file was initially included in gripper detection. After limiting detection and calibration to Left and Right, the full pipeline completed without changing the original file layout.

  1. Group filesLink one calibration and one demonstration
  2. Detect tags and calibrateCalculate the width range for each gripper
  3. Align time and posesAlign all three views to shared frames
  4. Build the replay bufferStore video, 3D coordinates, poses and gripper widths

The app exports files in a format compatible with the existing HoMMI processing pipeline.

June 9, 2026 · Processing results

One demonstration, 2,245 aligned frames

One calibration recording and one demonstration were processed to align video and motion from all three devices. The output is a Zarr replay buffer with 1 episode and 2,245 aligned frames. The saved file was read back to check video, depth, position, orientation and both gripper-width channels.

Developing the recording and processing workflow

  1. 06.05
    Recording and export across three devices

    Save video, depth and poses, then export in the HoMMI input format.

  2. 06.09
    Processing a complete set of recordings

    Produce 1 episode and 2,245 frames from one calibration–demonstration pair.

  3. 06.11
    Reusing calibration for the next demonstration

  4. 06.12
    Reducing recording stalls and missing frames

    Separate data recording from UI updates, then compare 30-second recordings.

Prepare file writers before recording starts

RGB, depth and ultrawide video are saved through separate tasks, with media writers prepared before recording begins. Gripper calibration starts only when ultrawide input and file writing are ready. Completed calibrations can be saved and selected again for the next demonstration.

Trace recording stalls in the diagnostic logs

On June 12, a Slave’s screen froze during recording and frames went missing. Diagnostic logs showed delays on MainActor, which handles UI work, growing from 2 to 7 to 13 seconds.

Delaying camera preparation only changed when the freeze occurred. Removing preparation prevented sensor status from being shown. Moving ARSession control to another execution context caused communication errors and freezes, so that change was reverted.

Data continued to be recorded for every frame; only the UI update rate was reduced. Pose display updates dropped from 30 to 2 per second, and shared-space status updates from 5 to 0.5 per second. Collaboration-data delivery and diagnostic logging were also separated from UI updates.

June 12 development notes · Left Slave, 30-second recording comparison
Record typeBeforeAfterMaster in the same comparison
Pose6091,8051,802
RGB50151151
Depth52151150

A 30-second recording was made before and after the change. Afterward, the Left device’s record counts were close to the Master’s. No MainActor delays or disconnections from the Master occurred in this comparison.

A brief pause remained when the camera was prepared again at the start of recording. Longer and repeated recordings were planned as the next checks.
